label: An Award requires an approved Decision
description: An Award cannot exist without a Decision that approved an Application (or, in funder-initiated giving, an equivalent internal approval).

label: A Payment requires an Award, typically with a Grant Agreement
description: A Payment cannot exist without an Award and, typically, a Grant Agreement -- though some funders disburse an initial installment before a fully signed agreement is in place.

label: An Installment's Payment Condition must be met before release
description: An Installment's Payment Condition, if any, must be satisfied before its corresponding Payment is released.

label: A Compliance Requirement attaches to a specific Award, not the Grantee in the abstract
description: A Compliance Requirement is always attached to a specific Award, not to the Grantee in the abstract -- the same organization can be in good standing on one award and delinquent on another.

label: Closeout requires both financial and reporting conditions
description: Closeout requires both financial conditions (all Payments made or the award formally reduced) and reporting conditions (all required Reports accepted) to be true.

label: An Amendment is forward-looking, not retroactive
description: An Amendment changes the Grant Agreement going forward; it does not retroactively alter Payments or Reports already completed under the prior terms.

label: A Grant Recommendation is non-binding
description: A Donor Advisor's Grant Recommendation does not itself obligate a Donor-Advised Fund to make an Award; the fund's sponsoring organization retains final legal authority over whether to accept it.

label: An active role must have an effective start date
description: A Role occupancy with status Active must specify Effective From -- a role cannot be considered in effect without a defined start.

label: A role's effective end date must not precede its start date
description: A Role occupancy's Effective To, if present, must not be earlier than its Effective From.

label: A role occupancy must identify its role holder
description: An instance of a Person Role must be held by a Person (via playsRole); an instance of an Organization Role must be held by an Organization (via playsRole). A role occupancy with no holder is not a valid occupancy, only a role definition.

label: A role occupancy should identify its context unless explicitly organization-wide
description: A Role occupancy should specify what it applies within (via appliesWithin), unless its Scope is explicitly organization-wide -- a role with neither a context nor an organization-wide scope is ambiguous about what it actually governs.

label: A Grant Term should identify which Award it applies to
description: A Grant Term should specify the Award it applies to (via Grant Term Applies To Award, or, for a Compliance Requirement, its own existing Applies To Award relationship), unless it is still in draft or unnormalized form -- an Award-less Grant Term that has completed normalization is missing the link that makes it actionable.

label: At most one primary Classification Assignment per resource and scheme
description: For a given classified resource (e.g. an Award or a Population) and a given classification scheme, at most one Classification Assignment should have Is Primary set to true -- multiple simultaneous primaries make Primary-mode reporting ambiguous about which classification the resource is chiefly attributed to.

label: Allocation percentages should sum to 100 when allocation is asserted complete
description: When a classified resource's Classification Assignments for a given scheme carry an Allocation Percentage, those percentages should sum to 100 once the allocation is asserted as complete. An incomplete sum is a data-quality signal to surface, not a gap to silently renormalize or complete on the resource's behalf.

label: Classification rolls upward through broader terms, never downward
description: A Classification Assignment's Classification Concept Code rolls upward through that concept's Broader chain for reporting purposes -- a resource explicitly classified under a narrower term is implicitly also covered by every broader ancestor. The reverse never holds: a resource explicitly classified under a broader term is not implicitly classified under any of its more specific descendants, since the source data made no claim that specific.
